baseline:
B
A standard transformer block is composed of a self-attention mechanism (often multi-head attention) followed by a position-wise feedforward neural network, which is a type of MLP.

B
A multilayer perceptron is defined by having at least one hidden layer between its input and output layers. These hidden layers use non-linear activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) to allow the network to learn complex, non-linear patterns in the data.

B
The MLP (or Feed-Forward Network) takes the output of the attention layer, which is a set of context-aware embeddings, and applies a non-linear transformation to each one, allowing the model to further process and refine the information learned during attention.

C
The MLP's weights are adjusted during training to learn associations. When it receives an input pattern (a key), its learned function transforms that pattern into a specific output (a value), thus acting as a distributed associative memory.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the learnable parameters of the network. The training process adjusts these values to minimize error, which is how the model encodes and stores patterns ("facts") from the training data.
